title: Opening, address and talk over photographs
summary: Interviewers note the date (June 1961) and address, then look through Clayton's photographs, including a recent group picture and a country picnic job, with mic hum interruptions.

places.name: St. Philip Street and Claiborne Avenue

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: I'll make a note on here first that we're interviewing kid Jimmy Clayton at his home, and the date is June the 23rd, I believe, is it? 1961. What is the address? How do you say the street? It's 3316 Leandes. Leandes.
Well, I don't know, that's just... Just comes natural. Just comes natural.
Yeah, that's holding it so hard, that right now.
Much better, that way. Yeah.
That's right. Some people have it down like they're blowing at the ground. That's right.

I always have my head up. That's a picture... Let me see, who took that picture? Did you take that picture? I was down in the country, went down there, and laid the droves down there. I forget her name. She had a moipery. And she went down there, a picnic where we played. That's way down in Diamond, Louisiana.
No, I don't think so.
I thought she went with us. Because we left, they met us right there at St. Philip and Claiborne, and we went in her car.
When was this? When about was this? How long was this? Let me see, it was around 56, I believe.
If I'm not mistaken.
No, I don't think it was. It might have been, but I don't remember. I wonder if it was Mr.

What was this other man, Mr. Just a second. Nick Allen. I don't even hear what you're saying. This Blaine machine is going bum. Remember the one that used to get a hum on it, Ralph? We sent the other mic away yesterday. It's working now, I see. Yeah, it's working all right. Yeah, but still look where it is when there's nothing on it. Everybody keep quiet just one second. See? Yeah, we got a hum on it. Got a hum on it again. Guess we'll have to go to the shop. Anyway, it'll pick up what we say, but there's going to be a little hum along with it.
Looks like you're singing a number here.
I am singing.
Oh yeah. I'm singing Don't Take My Gat Out Fishing.
What's that, a blues?
Just like a blues. It's got a brakes in it, and it's great. It's one of my makeup.

One of your numbers. That's a good picture. Let's see, if we go through these other pictures here. This is some of the old, you call this picture is Hummingbird Stomper. Yeah. This is John Hande. When was this taken? It looks like a fairly late picture.
This was taken last year. Yeah. We've got a group.

It's Alec Beegard and George Gayneau. Hande and Lester San Diego. Okay. Yeah, it's a very picture. There's one thing I might do here. I don't think it'll help much. Let me turn the plug. There's always a chance. I believe that helped it. Sometime a certain one of the wires is grounded better than the other. Oh yeah. Seems to be going better. Yeah. Okay, so we won't have to worry about it now. Sorry for the interruption. We have plenty of time. Sure. Let's see, what are we talking about again? Some of the other pictures there? Anything else to go through any of those pictures right off you? I don't think so. No, I guess not.
